Priyom —

Thanks for sending. The overall approach makes sense. A couple quick asks from procurement/engineering before we proceed: 

1) Sequencing/training tokens: we need the SOW language to call out per-model token allocation and a cap on pre-emptive training tokens (we can't have unlimited pre-training). Would you add a one-paragraph cap (e.g., 2M tokens/month for model training beyond inference)
2) Pricing schedule: procurement prefers a separate pricing schedule (Annex A) so we can attach it to our internal approval routing. Can you provide Annex A + a formal quote with tax implications?
3) Term and termination: legal asked whether termination-for-convenience remains at 30 days or if it's extended for committed capacity.

Looping in Mike (procurement) and Contracts. If you can include the Annex and a clean amendment for signature, we'll expedite on our side.

Thanks Priyom — I reviewed the proposed redline and noted a few items that need targeted changes before we send Annex A: 

1) Termination-for-convenience: suggest we keep 30 days but add a pro-rata unwind for committed capacity (i.e., customer pays for committed hours through the 30-day notice unless we agree to an early termination fee). This protects our unit economics.

2) SOW training token cap: I'll propose the 2M tokens/month cap Olivia requested and include an exception process (e.g., written approval by both parties for overage) so there's a path forward if engineering needs more during a model refresh.

3) Data & audit: add explicit reference to audit logs and data residency in the amendment if customer selects Dedicated/Private options. For the hosted deal, call out that audit logs are provided per the existing schedule in the MSA.

4) IP/derivative: minor language tweak to clarify that models trained on customer-provided datasets remain customer's IP; Redwood retains model-serving optimizations (operational telemetry) only.

I've attached annotated redline: msar_amend_redline_rishi.docx (comments in-line). Also: we need Sales Ops to produce Annex A with stepped pricing and a clear definition of "committed GPU hour" (how we measure, rounding rules, timezone for daily resets). Dev, can you produce the Annex and a brief line-item price calc?

I'll plan to turn this around by EOD tomorrow if there are no additional asks.

—Rishi
